uncited: This family covers specialized training configurations and optimization loops for Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) that deviate from standard baselines to handle specific input conditions or scene structures.

Unlike generic NeRF training, these pipelines integrate domain-specific constraints—such as physical exposure models for motion blur, generative adversarial frameworks for single-image synthesis, or coordinate contraction for large-scale stratified environments—directly into the optimization loop [BAD-NeRF](13523-bad-nerf.md), [Pix2NeRF Training Configuration](14803-pix2nerf-training-configuration.md), and [Strata-NeRF Training Configuration](#strata-nerf-training-configuration).
The number of samples and sampling strategy are hyperparameters tuned per method.
Strata-NeRF optimizes NeRFs for stratified scenes (e.g., multi-level buildings) using a specific configuration derived from Mip-NeRF 360.
It uses the "360.gin" configuration file, which employs a contract function to map input coordinates onto a ball of radius 2, handling large scenes better than the "blender 256.gin" configuration.
It uses a vector codebook in a "Latent Generator" network.
Choose this method for large-scale, multi-level synthetic or real-world scenes where standard NeRF configurations fail to capture global structure.
Size 1024 yields the best overall PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS across Coffee Shop, Bhutanese House, and Buddhist Temple datasets.
Method-specific training pipelines were developed to address limitations of standard NeRF training when applied to non-ideal inputs or complex scene geometries.
BAD-NeRF was introduced to handle the physical reality of camera exposure times, which standard NeRF ignores [BAD-NeRF](13523-bad-nerf.md).
Pix2NeRF was developed to enable single-image 3D reconstruction without multi-view supervision [Pix2NeRF Training Configuration](14803-pix2nerf-training-configuration.md).
